title: Epochal slab tiering and prefill synchronizer for paged KV reuse
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: On multi-tenant hosts with paged attention we observe recurring tail latency spikes during prefill phases caused by simultaneous decode waves that force repeated KV slot allocations and scatter-driven fragmentation. This increases per-token CPU/GPU overhead, lowers effective KV reuse, and occasionally triggers OOMs for heavy tenants. Goals: (1) reduce p95/p99 prefill + first-decode latency by synchronizing prefill admission without violating latency SLOs for short requests; (2) reduce KV fragmentation and small-slab churn; (3) allow kernel selector to prefer compact-friendly kernels when an epochal slab is active; (4) keep changes incremental to the runtime so Dedicated/Private customers can toggle behavior via config.

Proposed design: Introduce an Epochal Slab Tiering layer inside the KV allocator and a lightweight Prefill Synchronizer for admission control. The slab tierer groups small allocations originating from prefill into epoch buckets (epochs ~ 50-200ms window) and reserves compact slabs that are optimized for high reuse. The prefill synchronizer coordinates decode waves across worker threads on the same device to: (a) stagger prefill start times within an epoch so active slab pressure is smoothed, (b) advertise epoch-affinity signals to the kernel selection policy so kernels that favor contiguous KV layout are chosen when compact slabs are in use, and (c) emit a graceful fallback path that allows urgent low-latency requests to preempt with preserved KV references.

Key mechanisms:
- Epoch windowing: short time buckets used to co-locate allocations; windows slide and merge under heavy load.
- Compact-slabs: contiguous allocation region that the compactor will preferentially use and maintain a small free-list to avoid micro-fragmentation.
- Staggered admission: lightweight token-bucket per-epoch that gates prefill launches, tuned to keep decode concurrency within GPU memory-pressure budget.
- Kernel hint API: small runtime hint (epoch_id, compact_preferred) sent to kernel selector. Selector uses hint to bias kernels that are cache-friendly and do fewer scatter loads.
- Soft-evict policy: when an epoch completes, low-touch slots are demoted to a long-tail pool instead of immediate free to avoid re-allocation storms.

Metrics/Success criteria:
- p95 end-to-end prefill+first-decode latency reduced by >= 15% on median workload.
- KV allocation churn (alloc/free ops per second) reduced by >= 25% under mixed load.
- Fragmentation score (measured as free fragments per MB) reduced by >= 30% after 30 minutes of steady mixed traffic.
- No increase in median latency for short (<128 tokens) requests; customer-facing SLOs must remain within current bounds.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior: off for Private/Dedicated until enabled via runtime config (feature flag runtime.epochal_slab=true). For hosted customers, gradual rollout by region with metrics gating.
- Backward compatibility: kernel hint is optional; selector falls back to existing heuristics when missing.
- Observability: expose epoch metrics, slab occupancy, stall counts, and kernel hint adoption in Console under the runtime tab.

Open design questions and trade-offs:
1) Epoch length vs latency: longer epochs improve co-location but risk delaying urgent prefill work. We will start with 100ms and expose config.
2) Compact slab sizing: fixed-size vs adaptive. Proposal: start with a small set of slab sizes (4MB/16MB/64MB) and tune via telemetry.
3) Selector bias magnitude: too strong a bias may pick suboptimal kernels for some model shapes; implement safe caps and per-model overrides.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (prototype, 2 weeks): add epochal slot tagging in allocator, implement simple token-bucket synchronizer, add observability counters. (ENG + 2 SWE)
- Phase 2 (integration, 2 weeks): wire kernel hint path into selector, implement compact-slab freelist and soft-evict demotion. Run internal perf harness.
- Phase 3 (canary, 1 week): enable on low-risk region with runtime telemetry gating. Collect p95/p99 and fragmentation metrics.
- Phase 4 (optimize, 2 weeks): tune epoch windows, slab sizes, and admission rates; add guardrails for Dedicated customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for allocator tagging and demotion logic.
- Integration tests with simulated multi-tenant prefill waves showing reduced allocation churn.
- Telemetry dashboards created and baseline vs canary graphs attached.
- PR(s) merged with code ownership shifts noted.
